components.name: Instrument Bay
components.description: The standard surface for every panel and result.
components.css: .ds-bay { position: relative; padding: 20px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); border-top-color: var(--color-panel-edge); border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(155deg, oklch(0.205 0.018 258), oklch(0.165 0.013 258)); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 oklch(1 0 0 / 5%) inset, 0 18px 40px -24px oklch(0 0 0 / 85%); color: var(--color-foreground); } .ds-bay::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 6px; left: 6px; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--color-primary); border-left: 1px solid var(--color-primary); opacity: 0.55; } .ds-bay::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: 6px; bottom: 6px; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-right: 1px solid var(--color-primary); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-primary); opacity: 0.55; } .ds-bay-label { margin: 0 0 20px; padding-bottom: 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border); font: 500 11px/1 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; }

components.name: Status Badge

narrative.overview:
CentralIA looks like the instrument panel of a machine that is already running. The operator does not read a report about automation; they watch work move. A request enters on the left, crosses three closed checkpoints, and leaves as an audited execution — the motion is the argument. Density is high but never noisy: every surface is a labelled bay, every number is a monospaced readout, and the only bright colour on the screen means "this is moving" or "this needs you".

The palette refuses the generic neon-on-black dashboard by giving colour a job instead of a mood. Lime is the GO signal, amber is a person being asked, coral is a refusal, sky is information. Everything else is cold graphite with fine technical grids. Type is industrial: condensed capitals for headings, tabular mono for values, quiet sans for prose. Motion is material — a scanning sweep, a traveller on the routing track, a breathing status dot — and stops completely under reduced motion.

The sales area is a second, deliberately scoped voice: a counter-paper storefront inside the console. It opts in through `.shopfront`; its `counter-*` tokens and `.sf-*` classes stay inside that boundary. The shelf is a dense paper catalogue of sample goods and real tools, while the dark backroom reconnects the surface to the instrument world above. Adding the vitrine does not make the counter-paper palette a default for new screens.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument bays with corner ticks instead of soft cards.
Small radii, hairline borders, tonal depth.
Scoped counter-paper world for the demo storefront, never a console default.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Go Lime never decorates. It marks motion, the primary action, or a live value — nothing else gets it.

rules.name: The Status-is-Colour Rule
rules.body: Amber, coral, green and sky are reserved vocabulary. Never borrow one for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Scoped Counter Rule
rules.body: Counter colours exist only under `.shopfront`; never use them to restyle the console shell or imply a product claim is real.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Every number, timestamp, status and code-like value uses IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. If it can be compared, it must align.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No card floats at rest. Glow belongs to the GO state, not to decoration.

dos: Do lead with what is running
Do label every figure in mono
Do keep every `counter-*` token and `.sf-*` rule inside `.shopfront`
Do mark invented shelf figures as `sample`, including prices, discounts and percentages
Do keep the real calculators in the dark backroom with the console's own foreground tokens
donts: Don't invent zeros or percentages to fill a bay
Don't round panels like consumer cards
Don't add a second decorative animation when the telemetry already moves
Don't use Counter Red as a GO signal or borrow it for the console shell
Don't add hard offset shadows, consumer radii or raster product art to the shelf
Don't promote a demo price or discount into a real commercial claim
